jurisdiction.name: Chicago
jurisdiction.notes: City of Chicago, Cook County. Business licenses (food, liquor, Public Place of Amusement, hotel, mobile food) are issued by the Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) through Chicago Business Direct and the Small Business Center at City Hall, 121 N. LaSalle. Every license starts with a zoning review, and liquor applicants face ward-level moratorium districts and voter-dry precincts. CDPH handles health inspections; Cook County Department of Public Health only covers suburban unincorporated areas.

permits.name: BACP / Zoning Administration review of the business location
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Planning & Development – Zoning Ordinance Administration (via BACP)
permits.notes: Every BACP license application is checked against the zoning district before you can pay: Retail Food Establishment licenses are only issued at properly zoned non-residential locations, and liquor and Public Place of Amusement applicants submit floor and site plans for zoning sign-off. Look up the district on the city's interactive zoning map, and confirm whether taverns or entertainment are allowed, before signing a lease. Ask your BACP case manager to pre-screen the address.
permits.stall_risk: A location in the wrong district (or a tavern use in a B1/B2 district) cannot be licensed without a zoning change or special use, which takes months and an aldermanic sign-off. Get a written zoning pre-check from BACP before committing to a lease.

permits.name: Building permit – Express Permit Program or Standard Plan Review
permits.notes: Repairs and small projects go through the web-based Express Permit Program (which replaced the old Easy Permit Process in 2023); any build-out needing architectural drawings, such as a restaurant kitchen, hood or change of occupancy, goes through Standard Plan Review, where CDPH and the Fire Prevention Bureau review alongside DOB. Fees are calculated from construction type, occupancy, area and scope (use DOB's online fee calculator). Self-Certification by a qualified architect can shorten review for eligible projects.
permits.stall_risk: Standard Plan Review with multiple correction rounds is the longest pre-construction step for most restaurants. Use an architect experienced with Chicago restaurant filings, consider Self-Certification, and submit hood, grease interceptor and plumbing details in the first set.

permits.name: Certificate of Occupancy (assembly spaces and major rehabs)
permits.notes: A CO is required after construction or substantial rehabilitation of any Group A assembly space (more than 50 people gathering to eat or drink, regardless of floor area) and after major work on non-residential space over 10,000 sq ft. Pass inspections as work progresses, submit the online CO application near completion, pay any outstanding inspection fees and pick up the certificate before occupying. Spaces with 100+ public occupants also need a posted occupancy placard.

permits.name: Chicago Fire Department inspection (hood suppression, assembly occupancy)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Fire Department – Bureau of Fire Prevention
permits.notes: The Fire Prevention Bureau reviews hood fire-suppression and fire alarm drawings during plan review and inspects the installed system before the kitchen is used. Fire is also part of the BACP 'task force' inspection for liquor and Public Place of Amusement licenses, checking exits, extinguishers, occupancy and suppression service tags. Schedule the suppression acceptance test as soon as the hood contractor finishes.

permits.name: BACP Retail Food Establishment license (with CDPH health inspection)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) + Chicago Department of Public Health (CDPH)
permits.notes: Two-year license priced by floor area: $660 up to 1,000 sq ft, $940 to 2,500, $1,110 to 4,500, $1,320 to 10,000 and $1,650 above. Paying the application triggers the CDPH on-site inspection (food handling, temperatures, hygiene, pest control), which must pass before the license issues; new construction or build-outs also need CDPH participation in DOB plan review. Apply on Chicago Business Direct with the full DBA name, and have a City of Chicago Food Service Sanitation Certificate holder on staff.
permits.stall_risk: Failed CDPH license inspections (no hot water at hand sinks, missing sneeze guards, pest evidence) are the most common last-week delay; reinspections take one to two weeks to book. Attend a free CDPH inspection workshop and self-inspect with the Retail Food License Readiness Checklist.

permits.name: BACP Limited Business License (businesses with no food or liquor license)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP)
permits.notes: The general two-year business license for activities without a specific license class. Hospitality businesses rarely need it: a bar with no food operates under its Tavern license, any food service needs a Retail Food Establishment license, and hotels have their own license. BACP raised the fee from $250 to $500 effective January 1, 2026; confirm the current amount in Chicago Business Direct.

permits.name: BACP Tavern liquor license (bars where alcohol is the primary business)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago BACP – Local Liquor Control Commission
permits.notes: $4,400 plus a $40 one-time publication fee, renewed every two years; patrons must be 21+. After zoning approval and payment you have 30 days to submit all documents; BACP mails notice to voters within 250 feet, who get 35 days to object, and must decide within 60 days of a complete file (earliest issuance is about 36 days from payment). Task-force inspections by Health, Fire and Buildings (plumbing and ventilation) are required. The state ILCC license can only be filed after this local license is issued.
permits.stall_risk: Ward-level moratorium districts block new tavern licenses (and most transfers) and voter-dry precincts block all alcohol; no new tavern may open within 400 feet of an existing tavern in some districts or within 100 feet of a school, church or library. Check the moratorium and dry-precinct maps with BACP and your alderman before signing a lease.

permits.name: BACP Consumption on Premises – Incidental Activity (COP) liquor license (restaurants, hotels)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago BACP – Local Liquor Control Commission
permits.notes: For businesses where alcohol is secondary to food, lodging or another activity: $4,400 plus a $40 publication fee, two-year term, covering beer, wine and spirits. Moratoriums do not apply to restaurants seeking a COP. Same process as a tavern license: 30-day document window, 250-foot voter notice with 35-day objection period, task-force inspections and a decision within 60 days of a complete file. If the space is still under construction you can apply under conditional approval (decision within 90 days, one year to finish and pass inspections).
permits.stall_risk: Missing the 30-day document deadline suspends the file ($500 to reactivate), and neighbor objections during the 35-day comment period can lead to a plan of operation or denial. Assemble the document checklist before paying and meet the alderman and block club early.

permits.name: BACP Late Hour liquor license (open past 2 a.m., to 4 a.m. / 5 a.m. Sunday)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago BACP – Local Liquor Control Commission
permits.notes: Secondary license for Tavern or COP holders allowing alcohol sales until 4 a.m. Monday–Saturday and 5 a.m. Sunday; $6,000 plus a $40 publication fee, two-year term. Requires a site plan, floor plan and a late-hour petition, and new applicants must file an exterior safety plan (cameras, lighting, trained security) before issuance. Moratorium restrictions may apply, and the late hour privilege does not extend to outdoor patios.

permits.name: BACP Outdoor Patio liquor license (private outdoor area)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago BACP – Local Liquor Control Commission
permits.notes: Required to serve alcohol in a privately owned outdoor area next to a Tavern or COP premises: $1,760 plus a $40 publication fee, two-year term. Patios must close by 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday, and no live or recorded music is allowed outside. Seating on the public sidewalk needs a Sidewalk Café permit instead.

permits.name: Public Place of Amusement (PPA) license (live music, DJs, dancing; 100+ capacity)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP)
permits.notes: Needed for music, dancing or other amusement when occupancy is 100 or more, or when you charge admission or a minimum; venues under 100 with no cover are exempt, as are restaurants or hotels with an orchestra of eight or fewer pieces and no dancing. Fee is $770–$13,200 by occupancy plus $40 per fingerprinted owner, two-year term. Voters within 250 feet get 35 days to object, and PPAs cannot be within 200 feet of a church, school or hospital or 125 feet of an RS-1/2/3 district without a distance reduction.
permits.stall_risk: Distance rules and the 35-day voter objection window catch venues that planned entertainment late. Decide on occupancy and entertainment before design, check distances to residential districts, and keep capacity under 100 with no cover if you only want incidental music.

permits.name: Sidewalk Café permit (public way)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago BACP – Public Way Use Unit
permits.notes: Requires an active Retail Food Establishment (or Tavern) license, plus a liquor license if serving alcohol outside. Apply in the public way permitting portal with proof of licensure, insurance, a measured site plan and a sidewalk photo; a 6-foot clear pedestrian path is required. Permits run March 1 through the end of February and renew annually; the fee is set by café size and neighborhood land value and is paid after approval.

permits.name: Grease interceptor (Chicago Plumbing Code + MWRD sewage and waste control rules)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Buildings (plumbing) / Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago (MWRD)
permits.notes: Kitchens producing grease must install a grease interceptor shown on the plumbing drawings and inspected by DOB plumbing inspectors; the BACP task-force inspection for liquor licenses also includes plumbing. MWRD's sewage and waste control ordinance prohibits discharging fats, oils and grease to the sewer. Contract a hauler and keep cleaning logs for inspections.

permits.name: Sign permit (DOB + zoning) and public way sign ordinance
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Buildings + Zoning Administration; BACP Public Way Use / City Council for signs over the public way
permits.notes: A licensed sign contractor files the sign permit online with DOB; zoning review costs $200 per application for on-premise business identification signs, plus DOB permit fees. Any sign or awning projecting over the sidewalk or alley also needs a BACP public way use permit, which BACP turns into an ordinance for City Council approval (five-year term, billed annually); signs over 100 sq ft or 24 ft above grade need a City Council order.

permits.name: Cook County food service license (unincorporated suburban Cook County only)
permits.issuing_agency: Cook County Department of Public Health (CCDPH)
permits.notes: Reference only: inside Chicago, CDPH and BACP handle food licensing, so this does not apply to a Chicago address. Businesses in unincorporated Cook County apply to CCDPH by mail, with an annual fee based on seating that includes inspections, plus plan review for new establishments and a $40 county General Business License. Suburban municipalities (Evanston, Oak Park, Skokie, etc.) run their own health departments.

permits.name: Chicago Hotel Accommodations Tax registration (Form 7520)
permits.notes: Hotel operators collect a 4.5% city tax on gross room charges and file monthly through Chicago Business Direct by the 15th of the following month. Since May 1, 2026, hotels with 100+ rooms in the downtown Tourism Improvement District ZIP codes also remit a separate 1.5% TID charge (Form 7520T). Vacation rentals and shared housing units pay an additional 6% surcharge. State and MPEA hotel taxes are filed separately with IDOR.

permits.name: BACP Hotel license
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP)
permits.notes: Any building advertised as a hotel, motel or inn renting seven or more sleeping rooms needs a BACP hotel license; smaller owner-occupied properties use the Bed and Breakfast license and short-term rentals the shared housing registration. The 2026 fee schedule reportedly raised the base fee to about $1,000 plus a per-room charge; confirm in Chicago Business Direct. DOB and Fire inspect before issuance, and hotel restaurants and bars need their own food and liquor licenses.

permits.name: Mobile Food Preparer license (food truck cooking on board)
permits.issuing_agency: Chicago BACP + CDPH (vehicle inspection) + Chicago Fire Department
permits.notes: Two-year license for trucks that cook or assemble food on board: $1,000, plus a $100 Fire Department fire safety permit and a $150 fire suppression system review. Requires a three-compartment sink, GPS device, a commissary letter dated within 30 days, and liability insurance. Trucks may not park within 200 feet of the main entrance of a street-level restaurant (except midnight–2 a.m.), so plan routes around designated mobile food stands.

permits.name: Mobile Food Dispenser license (truck selling pre-packaged food)
permits.notes: Two-year $700 license for vehicles selling food that was prepared and packaged in a licensed food establishment; a $100 Fire Department fire safety permit may also apply. Needs a commissary letter and insurance, and the same 200-foot restaurant-entrance rule applies on public streets and on private property other than the host's. Carts selling packaged food use the separate Mobile Prepared Food Vendor license.
